source_text.body:
Self-host open-source apps by having an agent do the setup
The author has an agent SSH into a local server and install self-hosted apps (e.g. baby tracking, finance tracking), then set up a Cloudflare tunnel.
·
Nov 27, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The author opens an SSH link to their local server through a unix socket tunnel and lets an agent connect and handle installing open-source self-hosted apps, such as ones for tracking a child's feedings and diaper changes or personal finances. The agent also sets up a Cloudflare tunnel, replacing manual work in Cloudflare's web interface.
How it went
The author says it removes much of the friction of maintaining docker and config files, and avoids paying $5-$15 a month per app. No timings or failure cases are given.
Worth knowing
The author pays about $20/month for the AI subscription, sometimes $100 during big projects, and mentions a laptop-run local model as a free alternative.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
SSH into my home server at [server address and username] and install [self-hosted app, e.g. a baby tracker or personal finance tracker] using Docker, keeping its data in a persistent folder. Then set up a Cloudflare tunnel so I can reach it at [my domain or subdomain], and confirm the app loads through that address. Before you open anything to the internet, change firewall rules, or delete any files, pause and show me exactly what you plan to do.
Original source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50665117
